english: Fish is what I desire;
bear's paw is also what I desire.
If I cannot have both, I forsake the fish and take the bear's paw.
Life is what I desire;
righteousness is also what I desire.
If I cannot have both, I forsake life and take righteousness.
Life I desire, yet there is what I desire more than life; therefore I will not seize it by any base means.
Death I hate, yet there is what I hate more than death; therefore there are perils I do not shun.
If what men hate were nothing worse than death, then what would they not do to escape peril?
By this means one might live, yet there are those who do not; by this means one might escape peril, yet there are those who do not.
Hence there is what men desire more than life, and what they hate more than death.
Not the worthy alone have this heart—all men have it; the worthy are merely able not to lose it.
If given with insulting shouts, even a beggar on the road will not accept;
if given contemptuously after kicking, a beggar will disdain it.
Yet for a salary of ten thousand bushels men accept without weighing propriety and righteousness—what does ten thousand bushels add to me!
Once for very life I would not accept; now for the beauty of palaces I do it;
once for very life I would not accept; now for the service of wife and concubines I do it;
once for very life I would not accept; now for the gratitude of needy acquaintances I do it.
Can this too not be stopped?
His wife said: "You are handsome indeed; how could Lord Xu compare with you?"
Ji did not believe it, and further asked his concubine: "Who is handsomer, Lord Xu or I?"
The concubine said: "How could Lord Xu compare with you?"
Next morning a guest came from outside; sitting and talking with him, Ji asked: "Who is handsomer, Lord Xu or I?"
The next day Lord Xu came; Ji scrutinised him closely and thought himself the lesser;
gazing in the mirror at himself, he found himself far, far inferior.
At night, lying abed, he pondered: "My wife calls me handsome because she favours me;
my concubine calls me handsome because she fears me;
my guest calls me handsome because he wants something from me."
Thereupon he entered the court to see King Wei and said: "I truly know I am less handsome than Lord Xu.
My wife favours me, my concubine fears me, my guest wants something from me, and they all say I am handsomer than Lord Xu.

Now Qi's land is a thousand li square with a hundred and twenty cities; the palace ladies and attendants all favour the king, the court ministers all fear the king, and all within the four borders want something from the king: seen from this, Your Majesty is much beclouded.
So he issued an order: "Ministers, officials and people who face-reprove my faults to me shall receive the highest reward;"
"those who remonstrate by letter shall receive the middle reward;"
"those who criticise me in the marketplaces and it reaches my ears shall receive the lowest reward."
When the order first came down, ministers flocked to remonstrate, and the gate and courtyard were like a market;
some months later, remonstrances came only now and then;
after a full year, though one wished to speak, there was nothing more to advance.
